issue: Biblical United Monarchy; its historicity is debated (page says so), so the description should say 'according to the biblical account'. Start -1025 not verified; end should be c. -931 (start of Northern Kingdom, per Wikipedia).
polygon_comment: Plausible core, but the western edge (lon 34.1-34.4) lies in the Mediterranean (coast is about 34.5-34.8E) and the Philistine coast/Phoenician cities are included; the biblical realm also reached Transjordan and Aram, only partly covered.
corrected_description_eng: Kingdom of Israel (United Monarchy) under Saul, David and Solomon, according to the biblical account (historicity debated)
verbatim_quote: Whether the United Monarchy existed, and if so to what extent, is a matter of ongoing academic debate.

issue: Start c. -931 (Northern Kingdom began around 931 BCE), end c. -720 (Assyrian conquest) - row says -928 to -722, within a few years.
polygon_comment: Reasonable shape (Galilee, Samaria, parts of Transjordan only to lon 35.9), but the west edge at lon 34.2-34.4 is offshore and Transjordan Gilead is mostly omitted.
verbatim_quote: Around 720 BCE, Israel was conquered by the Neo-Assyrian Empire.

issue: Kingdom of Judah: start c. -931 (not -928); fell to Babylon in 586 BCE (page confirms).
polygon_comment: Covers lat 31.0-32.0 but extends west to lon 34.1-34.4, i.e. 30-40 km into the sea off Gaza/Ashkelon (those coastal cities were Philistine). The highland core (lon 34.9-35.4) is right; the Negev south of 31.0 is omitted.
verbatim_quote: Babylonian campaigns against Judah culminated in the capture of Jerusalem in 586 BCE

description_eng: Babylonian administrative zone around Jerusalem during exile period
issue: Babylonian rule ended with Cyrus in 538 BCE (-516 is the Second Temple's completion, not a Babylonian date). 'Administrative zone around Jerusalem' is not supported: the Babylonian-era province of Yehud was administered from Mizpah.
polygon_comment: A box of about 11 km x 11 km around Jerusalem; the province extended from Bethel to En-Gedi and Beth-Zur to Jericho (Miller and Hayes, per Wikipedia), so the outline is far too small.
corrected_description_eng: Babylonian province of Judah (Yehud) after the fall of Jerusalem, administered from Mizpah
verbatim_quote: The administrative centre of the province was Mizpah.

description_eng: Babylonian Exile - Jewish communities in Mesopotamia
issue: Dates acceptable (exile began 597/586, ended with Cyrus 538).
polygon_comment: Core Babylonia is lon 44-46, lat 32-33.5; the polygon runs to lon 48.8 and lat 35.2, i.e. into the Zagros (Iran). The 'Jewish communities' are not area-wide so a polygon overstates the area.
verbatim_quote: The Babylonian captivity or Babylonian exile was the period in Jewish history during which a large number of Judeans were exiled

issue: Persian rule over Judah c. 538-332 BCE is correct. Cited page (Second_Temple) is generic; Yehud (Persian province) is the better source.
polygon_comment: Outline (lat 30.8-32.2, lon 33.9-36.0) is larger than Yehud, which was a small hill province (Bethel to En-Gedi); includes sea and Sinai/Negev.
corrected_description_eng: Yehud, the Persian province of Judah (Achaemenid Empire)
verbatim_quote: Yehud... was an autonomous province of the Achaemenid Empire.

issue: Hasmonean dynasty ran c. 141 BCE to 37 BCE (independence/kingdom from c. 110; Roman conquest 63 BCE). Start -332 is Alexander's conquest, not Hasmonean.
polygon_comment: Outline (lat 30.7-33.2, lon 33.6-36.2) is a plausible maximal extent under Alexander Jannaeus, but includes sea and Sinai fringe, and is shown for 270 years of non-Hasmonean rule.

issue: Roman province of Judaea existed 6-135 CE; Rome conquered Judea in 63 BCE (client rule before). 70 CE is the destruction of the Temple, not the end of the province.
polygon_comment: Plausible (Judea, Samaria, Idumea, coast; north to lat 32.5) but includes sea and omits Galilee/Peraea that the page says were part of the province at its height.
verbatim_quote: Judaea was a Roman province from 6 to 135 AD

description_eng: Alexandria pogrom against the Jewish community
issue: 38 CE Alexandrian riots confirmed. Cited URL (Alexandria_in_Antiquity#Jewish_history) is a missing page; use Alexandrian_pogrom/riots.
polygon_comment: Small box about 10 km square around 29.9E 31.2N: matches Alexandria.
verbatim_quote: The Alexandrian riots were attacks directed against Jews in 38 CE in Roman Alexandria, Egypt.

description_eng: Talmudic period - Jewish centers in Galilee
issue: Cited page (Talmud) says the Jerusalem Talmud was compiled in Galilee in the late 4th/early 5th century at Tiberias, Sepphoris, Caesarea; it does not define a Galilee 'Jewish centres' period 200-500, so the dates are approximate and unconfirmed.
polygon_comment: Covers Galilee (lat 32.4-33.3) but the west edge (lon 34.6-34.8) is offshore, and Caesarea (34.9E) is not included.
verbatim_quote: The earlier of the two compilations took place in Galilee, either in the late fourth or early fifth century

issue: Academies existed (Sura 3rd c.; Pumbedita from c. 260; Nehardea destroyed 259); 200-600 approximate (Geonim to 1038).
polygon_comment: Pumbedita (Al-Anbar) and Nehardea lie near Fallujah (about 43.8E), outside the polygon, whose west edge is 44.2E; Sura is in southern Babylonia (south of the polygon's lat range, east of the Euphrates). Polygon misses the named places. Cited URL fragment '#Babylonian_yeshivas' not in page.
verbatim_quote: Nehardea was adjacent or identical to Anbar, a short distance from the modern city of Fallujah

issue: Jewish presence in Gaul from the 1st-5th centuries is documented; dates 500-1000 acceptable.
polygon_comment: Wrong area: lat 48.5-50.5, lon 1.0-5.8 is only northern France/Belgium. Early Gaul settlements (Lyon, Vienne, Arles, Narbonne, Bordeaux) are in the south and centre-east and are outside.
verbatim_quote: In the year 6 CE there were Jews at Vienne and Gallia Celtica; in the year 39 at Lugdunum

description_eng: Al-Andalus (Muslim Spain) - Golden Age of Jewish culture
issue: Al-Andalus lasted 711-1492 (page); the Jewish 'Golden Age' is typically 10th-12th century (ends with Almohads in the 1100s per page), so 700-1492 mixes two things.
polygon_comment: A single static polygon (lat 36-40.5, lon -9.5 to 0.8) cannot show Al-Andalus shrinking with the Reconquista; it includes the Atlantic off Portugal and the Mediterranean off Valencia, and omits Zaragoza/northern frontier at peak.

issue: Rhineland communities (Mainz, Speyer, Worms) were the centre of medieval Jewish life; 900-1200 reasonable (First Crusade 1096; Black Death 1349).
polygon_comment: Polygon (lon 5.8-9.8, lat 49-51.5) covers Cologne, Mainz, Worms, Speyer, Trier. Acceptable.
verbatim_quote: The Jewish communities of the cities of Mainz, Speyer and Worms became the center of Jewish life during medieval times.

issue: Medieval Jewish France ended with the 1306 Great Expulsion (with return 1315 and final expulsion 1394); 1300 end is approximate.
polygon_comment: Covers only northern France (lat 47-51); omits Languedoc/Provence/Narbonne, a major medieval Jewish area (Provence was outside the kingdom, but Languedoc was not). Overlaps with row 12.
verbatim_quote: the king condemned the Jews to banishment, and took forcible possession of their property

issue: Jews in England: reliably from the Norman Conquest 1066 until the Edict of Expulsion 1290; no community until Cromwell. Row 1000-1500 is wrong at both ends.
polygon_comment: Outline (lon -5.5 to 1.8, lat 50-55) roughly covers England but includes Wales and the Irish Sea side and part of Scotland border; Jews lived in English towns only.
corrected_description_eng: Medieval Jewish communities in England (1066-1290, until the Edict of Expulsion)
verbatim_quote: In 1290 King Edward I issued the Edict of Expulsion, expelling all Jews from the Kingdom of England.
